title: Certify v0.4.0: if a [[14,3,5]] stabilizer code exists, its monomial automorphism group has order 2^a 3^b 5^c — a certificate-backed exclusion of the primes 7, 11, 13
description: A certificate-backed structure theorem on the twenty-year-open existence question for a [[14,3,5]] qubit stabilizer (GF(4)-additive) quantum code (the [[14,3]] entry of M. Grassl's codetables.de, whose distance-4 construction dates to 2005-06-30): if such a code exists, its monomial (local Clifford x permutation) automorphism group has order of the form 2^a 3^b 5^c — no automorphism of order divisible by 7, 11, or 13 is possible. Proved by exhaustive, certificate-backed elimination of every nonzero symmetry class (cyclic; quasi-cyclic of order 7; orders 11 and 13; twisted classes), with exact-rational Krawtchouk linear-programming lemmas closing the fixed-qubit branches; every candidate distance-checked; independently re-verified by an adversarial referee with separately written code. THE EXISTENCE OF [[14,3,5]] ITSELF REMAINS OPEN AND IS NOT CLAIMED. NOT CLAIMED, AND CREDITED: the CSS case is settled by Koh et al., arXiv:2601.20927 (exhaustive CSS enumeration at n <= 14; their Table VI gives maximal CSS [[14,3]] distance 4) — an in-house CSS derivation is subsumed by their strictly stronger result and appears only as a remark crediting them; the automorphism question descends from Ball-Centelles-Huber 2020 (Research Problem 1); general stabilizer enumeration at n <= 9 is Cross-Vandeth, arXiv:2501.17447. Ships 43 SHA-256-pinned certificate files, the generators, an independent checker, and the classical code tables used; scope limits and unarchived intermediate runs are disclosed in the paper (sections 5 and 7). Three-lens adversarial review preceded release (log: qec1435-paper/FIXLOG.md; dated novelty sweep: SWEEP-RECORD-1435-2026-08-05.md). Computations carried out with Claude (Fable 5).
